messages:
alex: Heads-up: ran into inconsistent behavior across SDKs when cancelling streaming completions — Node abort vs Python/Go context cancel. Node sometimes leaves runtime waiting for finish, TCP connection stays open. Anyone seen this?
samir: Have you got a minimal repro? Are you calling AbortController.abort() during stream.read()? :eyes:
alex: Yeah, quick repro below. Trigger abort ~150ms after start and then await the async iterator — sometimes the connection hangs instead of teardown:

```js
const ac = new AbortController();
const r = await client.chat.completions.create({ model: 'gpt-small', stream: true, signal: ac.signal });
setTimeout(() => ac.abort(), 150);
for await (const chunk of r) {
  console.log(chunk);
}
```
zhao: Thanks — that matches something we've seen. In Node/fetch-land abort usually aborts the request body but the underlying http2 stream can stay open. Our runtime expects an explicit "cancel" RPC to trigger KV/cache teardown. If the transport doesn't send it, the backend keeps the session alive waiting for tokens.
maya: Context: Python uses asyncio websockets/cancels (CancelledError), Go uses context.Context cancel. Semantics are uneven across SDKs today.
samir: Proposed SDK change: translate AbortController/context cancellation into an explicit Cancel RPC to the runtime before closing the local iterator/stream. Make server-side cancel idempotent so duplicate cancels are fine.
alex: Sounds good. For Node I can patch the stream wrapper to call transport.closeStream(streamId) inside the abort handler. Quick question: should we try to drain remaining tokens (best-effort) before sending cancel or immediately send cancel?
zhao: For latency-sensitive UX, immediate cancel is preferred. But we can expose a small opt-in grace window like `gracefulAbortMs` (default 0) that lets callers wait 50-100ms to flush.
maya: Also we should document mapping: Node AbortController -> Cancel RPC, Python CancelToken / CancelledError -> Cancel RPC, Go context -> Cancel RPC. Add SDK integration tests asserting the runtime receives the cancel event.
ci-bot: CI: created linked issue #1221 and opened a draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-node/pull/456 :white_check_mark:
samir: :thumbsup: Can we also add an integration test simulating network partition where client aborts but transport reconnect retries — ensure retries do NOT resurrect a cancelled request.
alex: I'll add tests and the `gracefulAbortMs` config. Plan: alex -> node PR + tests, maya -> python docs + tests, zhao -> runtime handler idempotency + backlog task. Will post updates here.
maya: Small follow-up — in Python async generators cancellation raises CancelledError inside the generator; make sure we convert that into a Cancel RPC instead of swallowing it and returning partial output.
alex: Noted. Thanks everyone :pray:
